title: Rural Home Loans Escrow Cushion Base — Decision Table
content:
For a Rural Home Loans escrow projection, the cushion is figured on a cushion base chosen from the mortgage insurance months projected and the homeowner's coverage on record.

## Rule

The cushion is figured on a cushion base chosen as follows: when mortgage insurance is in force and its premium is projected for at least one and fewer than twelve months, the base is the projected property tax and homeowner's premium only; when the homeowner's policy expiry on record is earlier than the next payment due date and the premium of mortgage insurance is projected for twelve months or not at all, the base is the projected property tax and mortgage insurance premiums only, since lapsed coverage is placed and billed outside escrow; otherwise the base is all projected disbursements. The cushion is the product's cushion months twelfths of the cushion base, rounded to the cent.

## Decision table

| Mortgage insurance in force, premium projected for 1 to 11 months | Homeowner's expiry on record earlier than the next payment due date | Cushion base |
|---|---|---|
| yes | either | projected property tax plus projected homeowner's premium |
| no (premium projected for 12 months or not at all) | yes | projected property tax plus the mortgage insurance premiums projected |
| no (premium projected for 12 months or not at all) | no | all projected disbursements |

An expiry on the next payment due date itself is not earlier than it.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs, cushion months 2)

Projected property tax 2400.00, projected homeowner's premium 1200.00, mortgage insurance 50.00 a month.

| Situation | Cushion base | Cushion |
|---|---|---|
| premium projected for 4 months | 2400.00 plus 1200.00, that is 3600.00 | 600.00 |
| premium projected for 12 months, homeowner's expiry before the next due date | 2400.00 plus 600.00, that is 3000.00 | 500.00 |
| premium projected for 12 months, coverage current | 2400.00 plus 1200.00 plus 600.00, that is 4200.00 | 700.00 |
